A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe DOF-GS and contain readable methods, equations, experiments and figures. All pages were inspected, including v1's appended Figures 8–13; v2 ends with references. Separately referenced supplementary material is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original real and synthetic scene reconstructions, quantitative high-resolution comparisons, component ablations, focal-distance analyses and adjustable-DOF renderings.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction results in Tables 1–3, alongside focal-distance, CoC-mask and adjustable-DOF visual results.

M1.justification: The finite-aperture model, Gaussian blur convolution, learnable camera parameters, four-layer localization network and optimization components remain the same. Section 3.3's joint optimization becomes CoC-guided detail enhancement, and Ljoint becomes Ldetail, without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ma et al.'s real and synthetic defocus datasets for reconstruction and AiF novel-view synthesis, with higher-resolution evaluations on real scenes. The aggregate table added in v2 reports existing coverage; removing the explicit nine-scene count does not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds Deblur-GS to the corresponding visual comparison in v1 Figure 5. Deblur-GS was already named in v1, but had no displayed comparison results there. The other displayed comparators and the high-resolution comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported baseline-evaluation procedure changes from explicitly allowing published scores when implementations are unavailable in v1 Section 4.2 to stating use of released baseline code in v2 Section 4.3, without that exception. This does not establish that all experiments were rerun. Training remains 40,000 iterations, with the same resolutions, metrics and COLMAP-derived synthetic-scene inputs.

E4.justification: v1's qualitative component ablation in Figure 11 and additional focal-distance analyses for Cupcake and Tools in Figure 12 are absent from the supplied v2. The quantitative ablation and three-scene annotation procedure remain. CoC-mask visualization is retained through relocation from v1 Figure 13 to v2 Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Dataset averages retain the same reporting practice; manually annotated focal ranges are not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds aggregate PSNR/SSIM results for eight methods on both datasets, including DOF-GS results of 24.12/0.7667 on real scenes and 29.39/0.8914 on synthetic scenes. The full-model ablation SSIM changes from 0.7467 to 0.7667, while high-resolution results remain unchanged. v1 Figure 5's per-view scores and several appended visual result sets are absent from v2. Together these substantially revise the reported evidence, without demonstrating a general performance gain.

T1.justification: The thin-lens approximation, CoC equations, Gaussian-kernel approximation and mathematical reasoning are retained. Equation 14 expands the previously specified Pearson correlation into its covariance/variance formula; this is equivalent mathematics, not a new derivation or correction.

C1.justification: v2's abstract qualifies the training inputs as having moderate defocus blur, whereas v1 describes defocused inputs without that qualification. The principal contributions and capabilities remain: differentiable DOF rendering, learnable camera parameters, CoC-guided detail recovery and adjustable refocusing. Post-capture control mainly foregrounds an existing capability.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains why training on defocused images helps produce natural DOF effects, discusses reduced flexibility from global two-parameter modeling relative to per-pixel kernels, and identifies regions blurry in every view as difficult to recover. It also removes v1's specific explanation of Mip-Splatting's disadvantage relative to NeRF's smooth representation. These refine interpretation and applicability without changing the method.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly describes the reconstruction-loss combination near Equation 5, previously left unspecified there. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit count of nine real scenes. The CUDA/PyTorch implementation, network description, training budget and loss weights remain unchanged; the missing scene count does not establish a different selection.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around post-capture photography, adding light-field and multi-/coded-aperture approaches as alternatives requiring specialized hardware. It adds six references in that area and removes five references concerning single-image deblurring, defocus estimation or reviews. Related work now more explicitly distinguishes black-box deblurring from controllable camera modeling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental discussion are rewritten. Related work is reorganized into three topical blocks, joint optimization is renamed, and camera-model analysis and aperture/focus control move ahead of AiF benchmarking. This is extensive narrative restructuring despite the stable method.

P2.justification: v2 adds an aggregate benchmark table, relocates the pipeline and CoC figures, and brings v1's appended CoC-mask visualization into the main text. The principal comparison figure gains a Deblur-GS column and loses per-view score labels. v1 Figures 8–12 have no counterparts in the supplied v2, substantially changing the visual evidence and layout.

improvement.justification: v2 makes aggregate benchmark performance directly assessable in Table 1, changes the ablation SSIM so that it agrees with the accompanying discussion, and states useful applicability limitations. These improve transparency and consistency. Losing additional visual ablations, focal-distance plots and the explicit real-scene count reduces supporting detail, so the net improvement is limited.
